items.author: david_eng_mba
items.context: @david_eng_mba (26.485 seguidores, en inglés): dice que en el corto plazo $BTC responde a liquidez, tasas y apetito por riesgo, pero en el largo plazo lo que importa es qué parte del ahorro mundial se guarda en Bitcoin: 'el tope de 21M fija el límite, la adopción impulsa el alza'. Cuenta mediana con un post que despega (37 likes, 1.913 impresiones en ~1h50) y solo 2 respuestas; calza con adopción.
items.suggested_text:
The two timeframes even show up in different data. Price lives on flows, but adoption lives on-chain, and the two can move in opposite directions for a long time: over the last year $BTC fell about 32% and the network still added roughly 2.5M addresses holding a balance.

The long arc is the clearer signal: about 1M funded addresses in 2012, 10M in 2016 and 50M in 2023. Addresses aren't people (one person can hold many, exchanges pool thousands into a few), so the absolute number overstates and understates at the same time, but the slope is hard to fake.

That's the quiet part of "adoption drives the upside": with a fixed 21M supply, it's not just how many people show up, but how many of them end up holding their coins instead of renting exposure through someone else.
